clue.text: Perhaps tomorrow Rufus sets cryptic (Saturdays excepted)

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or obscured, so the letters of the fodder are jumbled

parts.note: the letters taken as written
S is the abbreviation for Saturday, so Saturdays stands for every S in the fodder, all three of which are excepted

explanation.surface: A note that the setter Rufus will supply tomorrow's cryptic, except on a Saturday.
explanation.walkthrough: Rufus was a long-serving Guardian setter, but not of the Saturday prize puzzle. Remove the three S's from RUFUSSETS and rearrange what remains, RUFUET.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomorrow is an example of time yet to come, so it lies in the future; 'Perhaps' marks it as an instance.

indicators.note: the division sign splits the word four apart, and the bracketed sum sits in the gap

parts.note: four spelt out as a word
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
one is the article a
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Reads as an arithmetic problem dressed up as a clue, with relish as its unlikely result.
explanation.walkthrough: The sum is not evaluated: each number becomes letters, with 1 as the article a and 50 and 5 as Roman numerals, and the division sign splits the word for 4.
explanation.definitionFit: Relish as a noun is a pleasing taste, a synonym of flavour.

clue.text: Number 10 receiving fine of no real value

indicators.note: receiving means the number word takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: ten written as a word
OK means fine, all right

explanation.surface: Downing Street, Number 10, accepting a payment that is worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: Number 10 suggests Downing Street, but here it is simply the word TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A token gesture or payment is nominal, made for show rather than for its worth.

clue.text: Bookworms are tipsy serving up wine and a little Scotch

indicators.note: tipsy means unsteady with drink, so the letters of 'are' stagger into a new order
in a down clue, serving up means the word is presented upwards, read from the bottom

parts.note: red is a type of wine

indicators.note: a little of Scotch is just its first letter

parts.note: first letter of Scotch

explanation.surface: Avid readers get drunk on wine and a dram of whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: REA from rearranging ARE, then RED read upwards as DER, then S from Scotch.
explanation.definitionFit: Bookworms are people who read a great deal, so they are keen readers.

clue.text: Shakespearean character's not large drunk male

indicators.note: not large means the letter for large is left out of the word for drunk

parts.note: blotto is slang for very drunk
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare figure described as a drunken man who is not big.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shakespearean character's' has the 's as 'is'. BLOTTO without L gives BOTTO, then M.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick Bottom is the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream who is given an ass's head.

clue.text: University objects when husband and son leave for trip

parts.note: OU is the Open University

indicators.note: when the two family members leave, their letters are taken out of the word for objects

parts.note: things means objects
H is the abbreviation for husband and S for son

explanation.surface: A university disapproves when the husband and son go off on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'objects' looks like a verb (protests) but is the noun THINGS; lose its H and S to leave TING.
explanation.definitionFit: An outing is a short excursion or pleasure trip.

clue.text: Emotional behaviour of cast with their acting

indicators.note: acting means performing a part, so the letters play new roles in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A theatre cast become emotional while acting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acting' sounds like the stage work the cast do, but it signals rearranging CAST and THEIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrics means exaggerated, showy displays of feeling, like histrionics.

clue.text: I break speed of sound after ditching ordinary engine

indicators.note: I break means the letter I splits the other word, sitting inside it
after ditching ordinary means the letter for ordinary has been thrown out first

parts.note: Mach one is the speed of sound

explanation.surface: Someone boasting of breaking the sound barrier with an ordinary engine left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: MACH ONE loses an O to give MACHNE, and I goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine is a mechanical apparatus such as an engine.

clue.text: Be naked and free

definitions.meaning: first meaning: wear no clothes at all
second meaning: have no engagements planned

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both wearing no clothes and having no commitments in the diary, two senses of 'on'.

clue.text: King's vehicle reversing in the other direction

indicators.note: a vehicle reversing goes backwards, so these letters are read from the end

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king
a cab is a vehicle

explanation.surface: The king's car backing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Back as an adverb means backwards, towards where one came from.

clue.text: Nato abandoning borders one time with difficulty

indicators.note: abandoning its borders means the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a means one
a stretch is a period of time, especially in prison

explanation.surface: NATO giving up its frontiers at a difficult moment.
explanation.walkthrough: NATO without N and O gives AT.
explanation.definitionFit: At a stretch describes something done only by making a special effort, barely managed.

clue.text: Good looking American robber

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Scottish for attractive, pretty
second meaning: ... Parker, of ... and Clyde, the 1930s American bank robbers

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a Scots adjective for pretty and the first name of the outlaw partner of Clyde Barrow.

clue.text: Scientist, one mistakenly called a monster, not honest about ego

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the remaining letters surround the self
not honest means the word for honest is removed

parts.note: Frankenstein is the scientist whose name is often wrongly given to his creature
frank means honest
I is the ego, the self

explanation.surface: A scientist misnamed as a monster, dishonestly self-centred.
explanation.walkthrough: Frankenstein was the creator, not the monster. Remove FRANK to leave ENSTEIN, and put I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein, the physicist of relativity, is the most famous scientist of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Fruit stolen for ammunition

parts.note: grapes are fruit
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: Stolen fruit used as missiles.
explanation.definitionFit: Grapeshot was cannon ammunition made of small iron balls packed together, like a bunch of grapes.

clue.text: Excite uranium in lump to make this

definitions.text: Excite uranium in lump to make this

indicators.note: to excite atoms is to agitate them, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: An instruction for nuclear physics: agitate uranium to produce a new element.
explanation.walkthrough: U plus IN, LUMP and TO are rearranged; the whole clue also describes how the element is made.
explanation.definitionFit: Plutonium is produced in reactors when uranium-238 absorbs neutrons, so bombarding uranium makes this element.

clue.text: Magazine to investigate many European leaders

indicators.note: the leaders of these words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A news magazine sets out to look into many European heads of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' suggests politicians but picks the initials of the four words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is the American weekly news magazine.

clue.text: Books about sport going over circuit

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the books are read backwards

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, books of the Bible

indicators.note: going over means turning over, so the sport is read backwards too

parts.note: RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: Books about a sport that covers a racing circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour is a round trip or circuit visiting several places.

clue.text: Hydrate corrupt London police here?

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Corrupt London police found taking a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yard is short for Scotland Yard, headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police; the question mark marks the definition as a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland Yard is the base of London's Metropolitan Police, informally called the Yard.

clue.text: Healthy wife cooks sole in residence

indicators.note: in means the cooked fish goes inside the residence

parts.note: home means residence

indicators.note: cooks means prepares or alters, so the letters of sole are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wife who keeps healthy by cooking sole at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooks' looks like the verb of the surface, with the wife doing the cooking, but it is the anagram signal for the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholesome means good for health and well-being.

clue.text: Provide milk for lost cat recently found outside

indicators.note: found outside means the word for recently surrounds the other letters

parts.note: late means recently, as in 'of late'

indicators.note: lost means astray, so the letters of cat are jumbled

explanation.surface: Leaving milk out for a lost cat that has just turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: To lactate is to secrete milk from the mammary glands.

clue.text: They suffer writing penned by smartypants?

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, so the writing sits inside the other letters
the question mark flags that the anagram signal is the pants buried in the single word before it, so the smarty letters are scrambled

parts.note: the word is read in two parts: smarty gives the letters, and the trailing pants, British slang for rubbish, says they are a mess
R stands for writing, one of the three Rs of reading, writing and arithmetic

explanation.surface: A know-all writes about those who suffer.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is buried in the one word: 'pants' (rubbish) scrambles the smarty part, and the R of writing, one of the three Rs, goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Martyrs are people who suffer or die for their beliefs.

clue.text: Foreign article on Tory peer doing away with hard competition

parts.note: le is the French definite article

indicators.note: doing away with hard means the letter for hard is removed

parts.note: William Hague, former Conservative leader, is now Lord Hague
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A foreign article about a Conservative lord stopping hard competition.
explanation.walkthrough: HAGUE without H gives AGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is a competition in which teams play each other over a season.

clue.text: Embodying the ultimate in style, an older model car

indicators.note: embodying means holding within, so the rearranged letters contain the last letter
to model is to shape, so the letters of the two words are reshaped
the ultimate in style is its last letter

parts.note: last letter of style

explanation.surface: An old car model that was the last word in style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' reads as a car model but is the anagram signal; the DeLorean is the stainless-steel car from the film Back to the Future.
explanation.definitionFit: The DeLorean DMC-12 is a gull-winged sports car from the early 1980s.

clue.text: Fancy Borgian clothing enhanced human

indicators.note: clothing means covering, so the two words wrap around the answer within them

explanation.surface: An elaborately dressed member of the Borgia family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' looks like the garments of the surface but signals that the answer sits within the words.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyborg is a person whose body has been augmented with machine parts.

clue.text: British bank close to German ex-chancellor

parts.note: a bank is a row, as of keys or oars

indicators.note: close to German means its last letter

parts.note: last letter of German

explanation.surface: A British bank comes close to a former German chancellor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German ex-chancellor' suggests Merkel or Kohl, but 'German' only gives its last letter; the chancellor is British.
explanation.definitionFit: Gordon Brown was Chancellor of the Exchequer from 1997 to 2007 before becoming prime minister.

clue.text: It gets a raise if it does its job well

definitions.text: It gets a raise if it does its job well

parts.words: It gets a raise if it does its job well
parts.note: reads like an employee earning a pay rise, but the raise is a cake rising in the oven thanks to a leavening agent

explanation.walkthrough: A raise sounds like a pay rise for a good worker; here it is dough or batter rising.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodium bicarbonate is a leavening agent that releases carbon dioxide so that cakes rise.

clue.text: Stone axes have zero rebound

indicators.note: to rebound is to bounce back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: X and Y are the axes of a graph
to have zero is to have no, nothing

explanation.surface: Stone axes bouncing back without effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded variety of chalcedony, a semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Maiden title included in new deal

indicators.note: included in means the title sits inside the rearranged letters
new means remade, so the letters of deal are arranged afresh

parts.note: Ms is a title for a woman

explanation.surface: A maiden's title written into a new contract.
explanation.definitionFit: Damsel is an old word for a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: Following retirement, group takes over pub game

indicators.note: retirement is a withdrawal or going back, so the whole is read backwards
takes over means the group surrounds the pub

parts.note: a set is a group
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: After retiring, a consortium buys a pub that hosts games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' suggests someone stopping work; in crosswords retiring means going back, so the built word is read in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket game played over a net.
